verdict.rationale: Bolt's docs describe a built-in Bolt Database that adds database functionality to your app without extra infrastructure. Supabase can also be selected during project setup as an alternative hosted SQL database, with auth and edge functions, so provisioning and wiring happen inside the builder. The one hands-on report (adding a sqlite database, then running out of tokens and hitting errors) is anecdotal and does not concretely contradict the provisioning capability. Missing for 10: detailed first-party documentation of how the provisioned database is wired into the app's code (schema/migrations, connection setup), and independent hands-on corroboration of a successful end-to-end provision-and-wire flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get a database provisioned and wired into my app without leaving the builder

citations.quote: Bolt makes it easy to add database functionality to your app without the hassle of extra infrastructure.
Use Supabase with Bolt to add a database, authentication, or edge functions to your app as an alternative to Bolt Database.
If you prefer to use Supabase when creating a new project, you can select it during setup.
Supabase provides: A hosted SQL database
